label: rem:blowup-local-cohomology-origin
title: Local-cohomology origin of the blowup at q=1
html:
The local cohomology connection. The local cohomology group H^1_{\mathfrak{m}_1}(A) at the unit defect z = 1 measures the obstruction to extending sections across the singularity. At q = 1, the defect locus \{z = 1\} is the entire base manifold. The substrate parameter is identically 1. One has:

  H^1_{\mathfrak{m}_1}(A)\big|_{q=1}
  = 
  R^1\Gamma_{\mathfrak{m}_1}(A)
   \neq  0.

This nonvanishing isolates the algebraic origin of the blowup. The \mathfrak{m}_1-torsion functor has a nontrivial derived functor exactly at q = 1, corresponding to regularity failure.

For q > 1, the defect locus \{z = q^{-1}\} \neq \{z = 1\} separates from the unit. One has H^1_{\mathfrak{m}_1}(A) = 0. The obstruction vanishes. Regularity holds.
